messages:
alex: FYI p95 latency jumped in eu-west around 03:12 UTC, correlated with sustained queue depth on the gpu pool.
maria: saw it too. p95 -> 420ms from 190ms. dashboards show batcher max_batch reached repeatedly.
cheng: digging into batch logs now, looks like a lot of max-size batches with high padding. sample: `pack_size=192 avg_seq=98 pad=38%`
samir: is this the continuous-batching path trying to pack everything? could be hitting max_batch and then queuing new requests instead of creating smaller batches.
jonah: yes, admission control seems to prefer bigger batches for throughput, but when requests are wide-variance it penalizes latency. we bumped max_batch up in feb for cost but forgot to add headroom for p95.
alex: ops-bot posted a deploy around 03:05, maybe rollout bumped config? can we confirm config change?
ops-bot: deploy: inference-config v2.14 -> v2.15 by @deploy-bot at 2026-03-18T03:04:12Z
maria: v2.15 increased default max_batch_size from 128 -> 192 and reduced per-gpu slot count. probably the combo.
cheng: logging snippet: ```batcher.admit duration=12ms queue_len=870 max_batch=192 batch_took=86ms wait=320ms``` — wait time is killing p95.
jonah: temporary mitigation: can we rollback max_batch to 128 or enable fast-fallthrough to form smaller batches when queue depth > X?
samir: rollback is safest short-term. alternative: tweak admission policy to cap wait at 120ms then force flush.
alex: agree rollback to 128 for eu-west pool and reopen postmortem. assign @maria to rollback + measurement?
maria: on it, rolling back config on eu-west now. will watch p95 and queue_len.
cheng: also propose we add a canary that simulates high variance sequences to our perf CI so this doesn't regress silently.
jonah: and add an alert for sustained max_batch occupancy > 60% for >5min. current alert only fires on GPU saturation.
ops-bot: rollback started by @maria at 2026-03-18T03:20:05Z
maria: rollback complete. preliminary numbers: p95 dropped to 210ms, queue_len down to ~140. keeping watch for 15m. :thumbsup:
alex: great. follow-ups: (1) perf CI test for variance, (2) admission policy change RFC, (3) retro on the cost vs latency tradeoff for max_batch increases.
jonah: I'll draft the RFC today.
cheng: capturing logs and trace links in the incident doc.
samir: adding a note to release playbook: remind to validate p95 with synthetic wide-length traffic before defaulting to larger max_batch.
alex: thanks everyone.
